newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ryanair says share market listing a logical move.
newsitem.headline: Ryanair says share market listing a logical move.

text.p: Irish cut-price airline Ryanair said on Thursday that a share market flotation would be a logical next step in its development.
"(A listing) is being considered but there's not anything final," Ryanair Director Ray MacSharry told Reuters.
"Obviously there is a 20 percent stake already held by Mr Bonderman and his group from the United States and at some stage there may be a logical follow-on that there would be a flotation," he said.
But he was unable to say whether any decision on the listing would be taken this year.
U.S. entrepreneur David Bonderman became Ryanair chairman last year after taking the 20 percent stake, which describes itself as the pioneer of the no-frills, low fares concept in Europe.
MacSharry was speaking after a news conference to present Ryanair's new service between Dublin and Charleroi regional airport, just south of Brussels.
The service becomes effective from May 1. Ryanair will also start operating on Paris.
MacSharry said that the lowest price for a return ticket was set at 3,990 Belgian francs, 79 Irish pounds, which he said was about half the price of the lowest available ticket.
He said Ryanair expected to carry four million passengers this year. The link between Dublin and Charleroi is expected to account for about 200,000. Ryanair carried three million passengers in 1996.
Ryanair will operate four scheduled services a day between Charleroi and Dublin.
The airline operates a fleet of 17 Boeing 737-200s.
It said it opted for Charleroi airport instead of nearby Brussels airport because it was seeking the lowest cost airport. In addition passenger tax was higher in Brussels.
